note: Plan 080/01 (camera director) verification run, taken by Claude on the dev machine, NOT by the user. Headless bench-harness (?loader=http-dir, DPR=2, Chromium/ANGLE-Metal) on the working tree with the director wired in; pak = build/original/opensa (087-ring rebuild, the same pak as 2026-07-24-ingame-617556f-087ring.json). ONE scene only (ls-noon). NOT pass-comparable to the user's in-game rows: different harness, and road cars registered 296 vs the in-game 1126 — headless boots with far fewer cars alive at bench start. The leg is vsync-capped (120 fps / 8.33 ms), so it cannot resolve a small CPU regression; it is recorded as evidence that the bench path still runs, draws the same class of frame (1181 draws vs 1238 in-game) and never touches the director (resolveCamera's bench branch wins, pinned by camera-director.test.ts). No BEFORE run was taken: producing one meant stashing the change under the user's live dev server, which was not worth the disturbance for a vsync-capped leg.

runs.note: After adding render interpolation (ped + car + focus drawn at lerp/slerp of the last two fixed steps) and turning the camera position weight back ON. Vsync-capped 120 fps, draws/tris identical to the pre-interpolation row — the lerp per drawn body is free at this scale.

microbench.what: one stepCamera call (look + zoom + mode rig + resolve), foot mode, no smoothing channels yet
microbench.where: node/tsx on the dev machine, 200k calls in 20 rounds after a 20k warm-up

microbench.what: the same call with the 02 channels live: input damper, planar spring + vertical damp + dead zone, steered-yaw channel, zoom damp
microbench.where: node/tsx on the dev machine, 200k calls in 20 rounds after a 20k warm-up
microbench.note: 2.4x the 01 seams — and still 0.0002 ms, i.e. 240x under plan 02's own 0.05 ms p95 budget. The follow rig is not a perf question.

microbench.what: the same call with the 03 composition channels added: heading tracking + turn-follow/idle recenter and the look-ahead offset
microbench.where: node/tsx on the dev machine, 200k calls in 20 rounds after a 20k warm-up
microbench.note: +10% over 02 (0.185/0.208). The whole director is still ~0.0002 ms per frame.

microbench.what: the same call with the vehicle camera live: the tuning-table substitution, the speed→distance and speed→FOV curves and the drift lean. Measured in BOTH modes in one run — foot is the control.
microbench.where: node/tsx on the dev machine, 200k calls in 20 rounds after a 20k warm-up, snapshots PRE-BUILT (assembling one allocates an object, a tuple and a Set — the host's cost, not the director's)
microbench.note: NOT comparable to the 01/02/03 rows above: this trace differs (it holds turn-follow armed every step) and the snapshots are pre-built, so its FOOT control reads 0.385 where 03 recorded 0.203. The comparable figure is foot vs vehicle in the SAME run: +0.16 µs (+42%), of which the per-step tuning-table spread is 0.061 µs. Absolute cost is 0.0005 ms/frame — ~100x under plan 05's 0.05 ms budget, so the vehicle camera is not a perf question either. Stable across 3 consecutive runs (foot 0.381-0.389, vehicle 0.537-0.555).

microbench.what: the same call with the additive motion layer live: bob, the landing dip, impact shake and the sprint FOV kick. The trace lands every 90th frame and crashes every 300th, so the one-shots are inside the measured path.
microbench.where: node/tsx on the dev machine, 200k calls in 20 rounds after a 20k warm-up, snapshots pre-built; `reducedMotion: true` is the control (the layer is still CALLED, it just does no work)
microbench.note: The layer costs +0.17 us on foot (+42% over the same rig with reducedMotion on) and +0.15 us in a car. Absolute 0.0006 ms/frame — the whole director is still ~1/80 of a 60 Hz frame's 1% budget. Stable across 3 consecutive runs. Same harness caveat as the 080/05 row: not comparable to the 01-03 rows, which is why the control was measured alongside.

budget: plan 080 ground rule 6 allows 0.1 ms p95 for the whole director (0.05 ms at the 02 stage)
